lines.japanese: どこかのビルの時計が１９時ちょうどを差して、時刻を告げる鐘の音が鳴った。
lines.english: A clock on some building pointed to exactly seven, and bells announced the hour.

lines.japanese: 「あっ、もうこんな時間か……そろそろ帰らないとマズいよね」
lines.english: “Oh, it’s this late already...? We’d better get home soon.”

lines.japanese: 僕は携帯を開いて時間を確かめるとそう言った。冬の甲夜は真っ暗だ。
lines.english: I opened my phone to confirm the time. In winter, even the early evening was pitch-dark.

lines.japanese: 「んー、そうだね、そろそろ帰ろっか」
lines.english: “Yeah. We should probably go.”

lines.japanese: と言いつつ、僕らの視線はある一点へ。机上に積み重なった紙の山。
lines.english: Even as we agreed, all our eyes converged on one point: the heap of paper piled on the table.
“Y-yeah...”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、月曜までに進めてくるって言っちゃったよね」
lines.english: “Haneda, you told her you’d make progress by Monday.”

lines.japanese: 「全然……進んでないね」
lines.english: “And we haven’t... made any progress.”

lines.japanese: 途中で何度か気にはなっていたけど、楽しいからつい言いだせなかった。作業は全くと言っていいほどはかどっていない。
lines.english: I had noticed several times, but we were enjoying ourselves so much that I could not bring myself to mention it. The work had advanced scarcely at all.

lines.japanese: 「うん、大丈夫……明日と明後日を使って、おれ一人で少しでも進めるよ」
lines.english: “It’ll be all right... I’ll use tomorrow and the day after and get as much done alone as I can.”

lines.japanese: 「ん……でも、それで終わる量……じゃないよね」
lines.english: “Mm... But this isn’t an amount... one person can finish.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ明日、学校に集まってやろうか？　図書室だったら使っても怒られないんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Then why don’t we meet at school tomorrow and work on it? We probably won’t get in trouble for using the library, right?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、明日は図書室使えないって。図書委員と文芸部が大掃除するんだって」
lines.english: “The library isn’t available tomorrow. The library committee and literature club are doing their big year-end cleaning.”

lines.japanese: 「タイミング悪いね……」
lines.english: “That’s unfortunate timing...”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫だよ、おれ一人でもなんとかなるって」
lines.english: “It’ll be fine. I can manage somehow on my own.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、そうは言っても相手は高内だし、泣き言が通じる相手じゃないからなー……」
lines.english: “Mmm. But you’re dealing with Takauchi, and she isn’t somebody who listens to excuses...”

lines.japanese: 「今日のこと根に持ってるだろうから、少しでも遅れたら本気で仕事を全部押しつけてくるよ？」
lines.english: “She’ll still be holding a grudge over today. If you’re even a little late, she really will force all her work onto you.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、根に持ってるってどういうこと？」
lines.english: “Holding a grudge? What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いい、いい、いい。うん、押しつけてくるってとこだけ理解してもらえればね」
lines.english: “No, never mind, never mind. You only need to understand the part about her forcing the work on you.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね……今日は進めてくるって約束しちゃったもんね」
lines.english: “True... I did promise her today that I’d get some work done.”

lines.japanese: 再び視線が机上に集中した。これ以上作業が増えたら、最悪、期日までに間に合わないかもしれない。
lines.english: Once more, every gaze settled on the table. If any more work was added, we might fail to meet the final deadline.

lines.japanese: どうしよう。かといってこれ以上付き合わせるわけにもいかないし、困ったな……。
lines.english: What should I do? Yet I could hardly keep the girls any longer. This was difficult...

lines.japanese: 「んっ……ええと……うん、どうしようかな……」
lines.english: “Mmm... well... What should we do...?”

lines.japanese: いつもなら誰かが出してくれる指示に従っていればいいんだけど、僕が班長なんだ。なにか言わないと。
lines.english: Ordinarily, I only had to obey somebody else’s directions. But I was the group leader. I had to say something.

lines.japanese: 「えっと……」
どうしよう。例えば明日も外でやりたいと言ったら、二人は付き合ってくれるのかな。それに外で会うとお金も使わせちゃうし。
lines.english: What could I do? If I asked to work somewhere else again tomorrow, would they agree? And meeting away from school would make them spend money.

lines.japanese: そんな図々しいことを言って二人に迷惑をかけるより、一人で寝ずに頑張った方がいいのかもしれない。だけどグレタガルドに召喚なんてされたら、丸々放置なんてことになりかねない。
lines.english: Rather than burden them with such a brazen request, perhaps I ought to stay awake and work alone. But if Gretagard summoned me, everything might simply be abandoned.

lines.japanese: 僕は俯いて黙ってしまった。こういうときにどうすればいいんだろう。クラブ活動もサークル活動もやっていない僕には分からない。
lines.english: I bowed my head and fell silent. I had never joined a club or any other extracurricular group. How was one meant to act at a time like this?

lines.japanese: 「んー、じゃあ、私の家に集まってみんなでやろっか！」
lines.english: “Hmm, then how about we all meet at my place and work on it!”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 僕がいつまでも黙っていると、渡来さんの明るい声が聞こえた。
lines.english: When my silence continued, Watarai’s bright voice reached me.

lines.japanese: 「場所さえあればいいんでしょ？　うちなら両オヤいないから、みんなでやろうよ」
lines.english: “All we need is somewhere to work, right? Neither of my parents will be home, so let’s do it at my place.”

lines.japanese: 「え、えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 僕は頭を落ちつけてから、渡来さんの提案を頭の中でまとめる必要があった。彼女の家で……なんだって？
lines.english: I had to calm down and sort out what Watarai had just proposed. At her house... what, exactly?

lines.japanese: 月曜までに作業を進めなくちゃいけない。だけど、それをする場所がない。だから、彼女の家でやる。
lines.english: We had to get the work further along by Monday, but we had nowhere to do it. Therefore, we would work at her house.

lines.japanese: なんだ、至極簡単なことじゃないか。はは、学校で出来ない作業を渡来さんの家でやるってだけで……。
lines.english: How simple. We would merely do at Watarai’s house the work we could not do at school...

lines.japanese: 「あはは、今日の夜に頑張って掃除しておかないとなー」
lines.english: “Ahaha. I’ll have to work hard cleaning tonight.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうなんだ……」
lines.english: “I-I see...”

lines.japanese: 「だけ」じゃない。渡来明日香の部屋に入る。こんな大事は他にないくらいだ。僕はしきりに額を手でこすった。
lines.english: There was no merely about it. I would enter Asuka Watarai’s room. No event could possibly be more momentous. I rubbed my forehead again and again.

lines.japanese: 「あっ、いや、はは……渡来さんがいいなら……」
lines.english: “N-no, ahaha... if you don’t mind...”

lines.japanese: 落ちつけ、みっともない。なにも特別な理由があるわけじゃなくて、たまたま作業をしに部屋を使わせてもらうだけじゃないか。
lines.english: Get a grip. This was pathetic. There was no special reason for it. She happened to be lending us her room for work.

lines.japanese: きっと渡来さんの部屋には、今までも色んな友達が遊びにきてるはずだ。なにも僕が特別なわけじゃない。
lines.english: Surely all sorts of friends had visited Watarai’s room before. There was nothing special about me.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そういえば羽田君は妹さんと大掃除って言ってなかったっけ？」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, didn’t you say you were doing the big year-end cleaning with your sister?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　んん……いや、そんな予定はないと思うけど」
lines.english: “Did I? Mmm... I don’t think we had any plans like that.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだっけ？　じゃあ、私の勘違いかもね。そかそか」
lines.english: “Really? Then perhaps I remembered wrong. I see, I see.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、じゃあ決定。何時頃がいい？」
lines.english: “Good. Then it’s settled. What time works?”

lines.japanese: 「ええとじゃあ、１０時頃に……」
lines.english: “Then... around ten?”

lines.japanese: 「おっけ。山科もそれでいい？」
lines.english: “All right. Does that work for you, Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 視線を向けられた山科さんは、少し考えるようにして目を逸らした。
lines.english: Under our gaze, Yamashina looked away as though considering.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん、９時から病院がある」
lines.english: “I’m sorry. I have a hospital appointment at nine.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうなんだ。じゃあ時間ずらす？」
lines.english: “Oh. Shall we change the time?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、先に始めてて。診察次第だからはっきりと約束はできないけど、間に合えば１０時に行けると思うから」
lines.english: “No, start without me. It depends on how the appointment goes, so I can’t promise, but if I make it in time, I think I can arrive at ten.”

lines.japanese: 「ん……そうなんだ」
lines.english: “Mm... I see.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、それまで二人きりで進めてて。きっとはかどると思うな」
lines.english: “Yeah. You two work on it alone until then. I’m sure you’ll make excellent progress.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 「二人……きり？」
lines.english: “The two of us... alone?”

lines.japanese: 斜め前の席からかちゃんと音がした。なにかと思えば、渡来さんがカップをソーサーに置いた音だ。
lines.english: A sharp clatter came from the seat diagonally across from me: Watarai setting her cup on its saucer.

lines.japanese: でも大きな音だったな……さっきまでは静かに置いてたのに。
lines.english: It was remarkably loud. Until now, she had set it down quietly.

lines.japanese: 「え、え、ちょ、ちょっと、待て待て待て待て。そんな、別に、きり、二人きりとか、そんなつもりじゃ」
lines.english: “W-wait, wait, wait, wait. That’s not—I didn’t mean for us to be alone together or anything...”

lines.japanese: 「二人きりだからって、今日みたいに話しこんだりしないようにね」
lines.english: “Just because you’re alone, don’t spend the whole time talking like we did today.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なんで他人事みたいなの。山科も来るんだよ？」
lines.english: “Why are you speaking like this has nothing to do with you? You’re coming too.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふ？」
lines.english: “Hehehe?”

lines.japanese: 僕は二人のやり取りを、他人事みたいに聞いていた。だって僕がクラスメイトの家に遊びに行くこと自体が初めてなのに、いきなり女の子の家に行くなんて。
lines.english: I listened to their exchange as though it had nothing to do with me. I had never visited any classmate’s house, and now the first house I visited was going to be a girl’s.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、じゃあ今日はこれで解散っ！」
lines.english: “A-all right! We’re finished for today!”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは立ちあがって紙の束をまとめると、自分の鞄に突っこんでスタンドアップを促した。
lines.english: Watarai stood, gathered the sheaf of papers, shoved it into her bag, and urged us to our feet.

lines.japanese: 山科さんも小さく微笑んで立ちあがる。僕はそれを見て彼女たちに続きながら、リフィルを一枚取りだした。
lines.english: Yamashina rose with a small smile. As I followed them, I took out a sheet of loose-leaf paper.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ところでおれ、渡来さん家の場所知らないんだけど、地図書いてもらってもいいかな」
lines.english: “By the way, I don’t know where you live, Watarai. Would you draw me a map?”

lines.japanese: 「そういうのは立ちあがる前に言おうよ……」
lines.english: “You should’ve said that before we stood up...”
